newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's doctor hero faces malpractice charge.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's doctor hero faces malpractice charge.

text.p: An Argentine doctor who became a hero for staying in war-torn Zaire to perform operations with a Swiss army knife was detained on arrival in his home countryon Monday on malpractice charges, local media reported.

Dr. Abel Pasqualini, who was recently named "Doctor of the Year" by the city of Buenos Aires, achieved fame at home after he ignored orders from his aid group Doctors in Catastrophes to leave the war-torn city of Bukavu despite the evacuation of other aid workers in October.

But the 46-year-old doctor, who was only persuaded to leave Zaire after he developed a serious pancreas condition, was allowed to go free after medical testimony that he urgently needed surgery. He was due to be admitted to hospital on Monday.
Pasqualini could face up to three years in prison if found guilty of malpractice in the case of the death of a woman during surgery in 1991, according to the state-run Telam news agency.

"This has caught me by surprise. It was a real blow to come to my country and find myself in this situation," Pasqualini told reporters, "But my conscience is clear. I am going to wait until the courts, in which I trust, resolve this."
Pasqualini stayed on in his makeshift surgery in the war-torn city of Bukavu even after it was ransacked by fighters and he had to carry out operations with a Swiss Army pocket knife.
The craggy features of the long-haired doctor became a regular feature on Argentine newscasts when a delegation from his aid group went to Zaire last week to persuade him to return home.

One of the viewers was a Buenos Aires judge who ordered immigration authorities detain Pasqualini on arrival in the country prior to taking him to his office to be formally notified of proceedings against him for malpractice.
